title: Worker onboarding with a clear finish line
metric: Illustrative workflow example; no client result claimed.
body:
> **Illustrative workflow example.** This describes a possible approach, not a completed client project or a promised outcome.

## Where work gets stuck

An account invitation can be sent while access, guidance or handover tasks are still incomplete.

## A possible improvement

Agree what ready means for each role. Track the invitation, acceptance, approved permissions and handover separately. Keep the approved worker record in its existing system.

## What to test

Test a normal start, an unaccepted invitation, incorrect permissions and a delayed start. Give each exception an owner and a next action.

## How to assess progress

Track incomplete starts, repeated follow-ups and time spent clarifying ownership before and after an agreed change. Agree the measures before implementation; no time saving or financial result is assumed.

## Scope and limits

The details depend on the provider's systems, permissions and responsibilities. This is operational guidance, not a clinical, legal or regulatory judgement.

title: Payment reminders with a clear next action
metric: Illustrative workflow example; no client result claimed.
body:
> **Illustrative workflow example.** This describes a possible approach, not a completed client project or a promised outcome.

## Where work gets stuck

A reminder may arrive without the file, instructions or contact a worker needs to act.

## A possible improvement

Agree the payment preparation steps and responsibilities. Link to the approved information location, explain the required action and route questions to a named role.

## What to test

Test missing information, an inaccessible link, a disputed item and a late response. Keep payment approvals with the authorised people.

## How to assess progress

Compare repeated questions, missing inputs and unresolved exceptions using an agreed baseline. Agree the measures before implementation; no time saving or financial result is assumed.

## Scope and limits

The details depend on the provider's systems, permissions and responsibilities. This is operational guidance, not a clinical, legal or regulatory judgement.

title: Follow-up actions with visible ownership
metric: Illustrative workflow example; no client result claimed.
body:
> **Illustrative workflow example.** This describes a possible approach, not a completed client project or a promised outcome.

## Where work gets stuck

An action recorded in meeting notes can become difficult to find or follow through.

## A possible improvement

Record the action, accountable owner, due date and review point in an approved operational view. Link to the authorised record without duplicating sensitive details.

## What to test

Test overdue actions, an absent owner and an action needing escalation. Closure should require the appropriate person to review the outcome.

## How to assess progress

Check overdue actions, unassigned work and time spent finding the current status. Agree the measures before implementation; no time saving or financial result is assumed.

## Scope and limits

The details depend on the provider's systems, permissions and responsibilities. This is operational guidance, not a clinical, legal or regulatory judgement.
